findings.element: Section 2 condition row — the On the invoice target select, when Comparison is is empty or is not empty
findings.finding: For the two operands that read only the invoice side, the prototype disables the On the invoice target select and leaves the ignored On the payment source select editable, and the engine still resolves that unread source — so the row is discarded as not applicable whenever the payment lacks the source field.
findings.user_impact: Two of the ten operands R5 mandates are unusable: a rule reading Memo on statement is empty cannot be pointed at Invoice number instead, and on the FDD own example B it returns No match even though the sole candidate TW-5510 has an empty memo and satisfies the condition.
findings.suggested_fix: Invert the gating for value-less operands — keep the On the invoice target enabled and disable the On the payment source instead — and skip the resolve()/absent check for the source on those rows so applicability is judged on the field the row actually reads.

evidence.quote: Condition “Invoice note” is absent on this SalesReceipt → row skipped, not applicable. / Every configured condition is not applicable → NOT scope-only. Process as usual.
evidence.source: R5 (all ten operands) + R6 (condition rows may target DocNumber or PrivateNote) + R14 (absent = skipped, applied to the field the row reads)

findings.element: Overlay footer Save button and its message, with the master switch off
findings.finding: Validation runs regardless of the master switch, so a retained configuration that carries a blocking error keeps Save disabled after the engine is switched off, with the error message pointing at fields that are no longer rendered.
findings.user_impact: Switching the rule off cannot be committed — the user sees 1 thing to fix before this can be saved. with sections 1-3 hidden and zero error fields on screen, so the integration cannot be returned to the default matcher without first re-enabling the rule and repairing a configuration they intend to disable.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate validate() on the engine-on flag so that only an enabled rule blocks Save, leaving the off state always saveable while the configuration is still retained.

evidence.quote: 1 thing to fix before this can be saved.
evidence.source: R21 / S1.5 — switching the engine off returns that integration to the default matcher AND retains the configuration

findings.element: Section 2 condition box on first turn-on, vs the reference card What Synder does today, by default
findings.finding: The reference card states that nothing is pre-filled, but flipping the master switch reveals a ready-made rule — all three scope rows on and a fully authored condition row the user never chose.
findings.user_impact: A user who enables the rule and saves immediately gets a narrower rule than the default matcher they were told they are replacing, and the on-screen claim that nothing is pre-filled is false at the moment it matters.
findings.suggested_fix: Start section 2 as an empty condition box (the state R16 already defines) so first turn-on presents scope defaults only, or drop the sentence and state exactly what the starting rule contains.

evidence.quote: Nothing is pre-filled, so no existing configuration changes until you build a rule and save it.
evidence.source: R20 / S1.1 — on first open no configuration is pre-filled

findings.element: Section 1 invoice-number row hint, and the same sentence on the condition row when the target is Invoice number
findings.finding: Both hints state the DocNumber limit as a fixed length rather than a maximum, describing the field as holding 21 characters where the spec defines at most 21.
findings.user_impact: The stated rule reads as though every invoice number is 21 characters long, which misdescribes when truncation actually bites.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword both hints to hold at most 21 characters while keeping the existing truncation sentence.

evidence.quote: The invoice number holds 21 characters; a longer reference is shortened to 21 on both sides before comparing.
evidence.source: R13 — DocNumber holds at most 21 characters; the limit and truncation must be stated on the field

reference_gaps: No Figma frames exist for this feature — the reference is a text spec only. Layout, spacing, hierarchy and component styling are unassessable; only presence, labels, component types and required states were checkable.
R27 requires a marketable name but the FDD supplies none (flagged A0).
Q3 leaves default N, maximum N and the page ceiling unresolved, so 90 / 365 could not be checked (flagged A3).
R20 requires non-editable default-behaviour text but supplies no wording (flagged A1).
Q4 leaves Generic-customer behaviour unresolved, so only the presence of a warning was checkable (flagged A2).
R11 does not say how a disabled off-switch should be presented, so only its functional immovability was checked.
Q1 and Q2 mark case-insensitivity and the truncation as unconfirmed, so both were checked only against R13 as written.
The spec defines no loading, saving or post-save confirmation state, so their absence is not reportable.
gaps: The state map records outcomes only for the simple-charge and overpayment samples; example C and the cancel-sync-on outcome have no recorded verdict, so the prototype was exercised directly to confirm R17 three branches.

The state map records cancel-sync as a shared value but not its commit semantics: the overlay copy is transactional while the GSP toggle commits instantly. One value, two commit models — below my confidence floor as an R18 violation, but unrecorded and worth a decision.
The state map lists target_disabled_when_is_empty as a bare fact with no verdict; interrogating it produced FID-1.
The engine-off-with-a-retained-validation-error path appears in neither the exercised controls nor not_exercised; it was reached manually.
file:// and localhost navigation were blocked by browser policy, so live verification ran against the deployed copy after confirming it is byte-identical to the local file.
